newsitem.title: GREECE: Ample liquidity drives Greek depos down, bonds up.
newsitem.headline: Ample liquidity drives Greek depos down, bonds up.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were softer on excess interbank liquidity in late dealings fuelling an advance in non-taxable fixed coupon bonds and FRNs, dealers said.
Ecu/drachma was locked in the 307.0/30 range, currently trading around 307.11/16 after opening low at 307.0/15, dealers said.
"The market is calm with depos and forex forwards trading lower because of excess liquidity," said a private bank dealer.
The lower funding cost was the driving force behind a mini-rally in non-taxable fixed coupon bonds and FRNs due 2002 today, bond dealers said.

"Some buying interest for non-taxable fixed coupon bonds and FRNs due 2002 from local investors pushed their prices up 10 to 15 basis points," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. "It must be entirely related to the lower interbank rates and funding cost."
The mark was quoted at 157.11/21 from Thursday's 157.095 fix, the dollar at 269.43/53 drachmas from 269.910 and the ecu at 307.06/16 from 307.090 drachmas.
The National Bank of Greece, the domestic money market's biggest player, quoted the following late rates:
** Six months at 10.25-10.75 ** Nine months at 10.25-10.75
